title: Serial Cell-free DNA Assessments in Preclinical Models
author: Rostami, Yu, et al.
materials: Sso Advanced Universal SYBR Green Supermix

steps.title: Plan sample batch size
steps.instruction: Decide how many plasma samples to process (recommended 20–40, maximum 70) and avoid using the full 96‑well block to prevent samples sitting too long.

steps.title: Prepare PBS‑EDTA topping solution
steps.instruction: Make 1× Phosphate Buffer Solution (PBS) with 0.5 mM EDTA; calculate the total volume needed to bring each plasma sample to 200 µL (e.g., for 200 samples each 75 µL plasma, mix 24.75 mL 1× PBS with 25 µL 0.5 M EDTA to obtain 25 mL of topping solution).

steps.title: Print sample layout and label tubes
steps.instruction: Print a sheet listing sample IDs, original plasma volumes, and required PBS‑EDTA topping volumes; also print the 96‑well layout. Label collection microtubes (e.g., 1–8, 9–16, …) and elution tubes in advance.

steps.title: Set oven and wear mask
steps.instruction: Set a dry oven (or incubator) to 60 °C and wear a surgical mask at all times to minimise human DNA contamination.

steps.title: Thaw plasma and add proteinase K
steps.instruction: Remove plasma samples from –80 °C and thaw on ice. While thawing, add 20 µL proteinase K to the bottom of each collection microtube (blue rack).

steps.title: Top up plasma to 200 µL
steps.instruction: Once thawed, add the calculated volume of 1× PBS + 0.5 mM EDTA to each plasma sample so the total volume equals 200 µL. Keep tubes at 20–25 °C.

steps.title: Transfer plasma to collection tubes
steps.instruction: Add the entire 200 µL plasma (now topped up) to the corresponding proteinase‑K‑containing microtube, pipetting near the bottom to avoid loss. Ensure tubes remain labelled (1–8, 9–16, …).

steps.title: Add Buffer ACL and cap
steps.instruction: Using an 8‑channel multichannel pipette, add 200 µL Buffer ACL (without RNase carrier) to each tube. Cap tubes carefully and wrap each 8‑strip with plastic cling wrap to prevent spills.

steps.title: Vortex and centrifuge
steps.instruction: Vortex each 8‑strip for 15 s, keeping a hand on the caps. Remove cling wrap, place tubes back in the rack, balance the rack (weigh and adjust with water), and centrifuge at 3 468 × g for 1 min to collect liquid from caps.

steps.title: Incubate at 60 °C
steps.instruction: Wrap the strips again with cling wrap and place them in the 60 °C oven for 30 min. (An incubator may be used; a water bath has not been tested.)

steps.title: Second vortex, add Buffer ACB
steps.instruction: Vortex the strips again for 15 s, then set the oven to 56 °C. Uncap tubes (caps upwards) and add 200 µL Buffer ACB with an 8‑channel pipette.

steps.title: Vortex, ice, and centrifuge
steps.instruction: Vortex the tubes, place them on ice for 5 min, then balance and centrifuge at 3 468 × g for 1 min (same precautions as before).

steps.title: Set up vacuum manifold
steps.instruction: Assemble the NucleoVac 96 Vacuum Manifold with square‑block spacer, S‑block waste collector, lid, and place the QIAamp 96 plate on top. If any wells are unused, cover them with a plastic seal.

steps.title: Transfer lysate to QIAamp plate
steps.instruction: Apply the entire mixture from each collection microtube (≈620 µL) to the corresponding well of the QIAamp 96 plate. Use a P1000 pipette for the bulk transfer, then a P200 for any residual volume. Begin aspirating when the tip contacts the liquid to avoid overflow.

steps.title: Bind DNA with vacuum
steps.instruction: Seal the QIAamp 96 plate with an AirPore Tape sheet, turn on the vacuum, and allow the lysate to flow through the columns for DNA binding (apply gentle pressure if needed to obtain a seal).

steps.title: Remove plate and empty waste
steps.instruction: Carefully lift the QIAamp 96 plate from the manifold and place it between two tip boxes to avoid contamination. Empty the flow‑through waste from the S‑block using an aspirator.

steps.title: Wash with Buffer AW1
steps.instruction: Return the plate to the manifold. Add 500 µL Buffer AW1 to each well using an 8‑channel pipette (recommended as two 250 µL additions with a 300 µL multichannel). Apply vacuum as in step 13.

steps.title: Wash with Buffer AW2
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL Buffer AW2 to each well (again as two 250 µL additions with a 300 µL multichannel) and repeat the vacuum step.

steps.title: Final washes and centrifuge
steps.instruction: Repeat the vacuum wash steps (as in steps 14–15) once more. Then remove the S‑block, place the QIAamp plate directly on top of the S‑block, weigh and balance the assembly, and centrifuge at 3 468 × g for 10 min.

steps.title: Dry plate at 56 °C
steps.instruction: Remove the plate from the S‑block, place it between two tip boxes, and incubate in the 56 °C oven for 10 min (ensure enough bench space and balance with tip boxes).

steps.title: Elute cfDNA
steps.instruction: Position the QIAamp plate over a rack of pre‑labelled elution microtubes. Add 100 µL EB buffer (20–25 °C) to each well using an 8‑channel pipette, aiming for the centre of the well. Seal with a fresh AirPore Tape sheet and incubate 10 min at 20–25 °C.

steps.title: Collect eluate
steps.instruction: Weigh and balance the plate with the elution tubes, then centrifuge at 3 468 × g for 12 min. Transfer the entire eluate (≈80–90 µL, typically ~85 µL) from each tube into new pre‑labelled tubes. Record the exact volume if possible and store the purified cfDNA at –20 °C. Use 8‑strip PCR tubes for storage.
